trust_decision.summary: Which local user an inbound signed SAML assertion links to (USERNAME_LINK/EMAIL_LINK) is decided from values read out of the signed NameID/AttributeValue elements; these must be read in full (itertext) so they equal what exc-c14n signed, not truncated at an XML comment via .text.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'SAML NameID comment truncation'; _get_name_id is the NameID reader, and it already uses itertext at the pinned commit (fixed by prior CVE-2026-40165), so it looks already safe.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST SAML ACS view of a SAML source (authentik/sources/saml/views.py) -> ResponseProcessor.prepare_flow_manager -> SourceFlowManager -> SourceMapper.get_base_properties -> SAMLSource.get_base_user_properties (username)
same ACS route, AttributeValue loop in SAMLSource.get_base_user_properties (attributes incl. groups, mail)
same ACS route, ResponseProcessor._get_name_id (refactor only: inline itertext replaced by shared helper)
new shared helper authentik/common/saml/utils.py get_element_text, used by the two sites above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both real sites sit in SAMLSource.get_base_user_properties (authentik/sources/saml/models.py:221-244), a property producer one file away from the processor; it is a producer (O7), not a separate implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The NameID identifier at authentik/sources/saml/processors/response.py:296 already uses itertext (previous CVE fix, regression test at authentik/sources/saml/tests/test_response.py:312), so a solver can argue the comment truncation is already fixed and that attribute values only feed admin property mappings, not matching.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Multi-valued attributes must stay lists and the SAML groups attribute must be renamed to 'groups' and left unflattened, while other single values are flattened; legitimate NameIDs and transient NameID handling must keep working. An over-broad fix (rejecting any response containing a comment anywhere, or changing list handling) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: NameID text with an embedded XML comment (username property)
AttributeValue text with an embedded comment, multi-valued attributes (list of values)
groups attribute values (kept as list, not flattened)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a signed Issuer or SessionIndex read with .text from the assertion and used for source selection or session binding
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same processor already reads other assertion children; a maintainer adding issuer validation would naturally write element.text as at authentik/sources/saml/processors/response.py:227.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: transient-user path building the username from name_id_el.text instead of the itertext identifier
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Transient path receives both the element and the string; the string/element split is exactly how the published bug arose.

O9_family: parser differential (XML comment truncation vs exc-c14n signature canonicalization) leading to identity confusion / account takeover

O10_build.toolchain: uv / pyproject.toml, lxml, xmlsec (libxmlsec1 native lib)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change only attributes['username'] = name_id.text at models.py:242 (or conclude _get_name_id is already fixed) and leave the AttributeValue loop at models.py:233 on .text.

out_of_scope_notes: Provider-side LogoutRequest parser reads NameID/SessionIndex with .text (authentik/providers/saml/processors/logout_request_parser.py:57,67) but does no signature check there and the advisory excludes the Provider role.
Windows NameID format splits on backslash (authentik/sources/saml/processors/response.py:311-314); _get_name_id_filter appears unused, not pursued.
Custom admin property mappings receive the raw name_id element and assertion and may themselves use .text; admin code, not project code.
